distillation_scope.leaf_granularity: First-layer clinical disease leaf for atrial fibrillation, without splitting by paroxysmal, persistent, valvular, postoperative, thyroid-related, heart-failure-related, or trigger-associated context.
distillation_scope.subtype_policy: Temporal pattern, reversible triggers, structural substrate, thromboembolic risk, bleeding context, rate-control tolerance, rhythm-control feasibility, and left atrial appendage intervention context are represented as axes, risk factors, treatment modifiers, and mechanisms rather than disease-name qualifiers.
distillation_scope.ranking_note: Presentation ranking should use ECG evidence of atrial fibrillation, absent discrete P waves, irregularly irregular R-R intervals, ventricular rate, symptom and hemodynamic response, structural substrate, reversible triggers, and thromboembolic or bleeding context. Treatment response and follow-up rhythm status should remain treatment-simulation or post-workup evidence unless explicitly consumed by that mode.

latent_mechanisms.clinical_meaning: Disorganized atrial activation replaces coordinated sinus atrial depolarization, producing no discrete P waves and an atrial fibrillatory baseline.

latent_mechanisms.display_name: Pulmonary vein trigger and atrial reentry activity
latent_mechanisms.clinical_meaning: Focal atrial triggers and reentry-supporting atrial conduction heterogeneity initiate and sustain atrial fibrillation episodes.
Left atrial dilation, fibrosis, pressure or volume load, valvular disease, hypertension, cardiomyopathy, or aging create a durable substrate for recurrent or sustained atrial fibrillation.
Adrenergic or vagal tone shifts alter atrial refractoriness and AV nodal conduction, changing episode onset, symptoms, and ventricular response.
Variable conduction through the AV node transmits an irregular ventricular rhythm; when conduction is rapid, filling time shortens and symptoms or instability can emerge.

latent_mechanisms.display_name: Atrial contraction loss and low-output pressure
latent_mechanisms.clinical_meaning: Loss of coordinated atrial contraction and irregular ventricular filling reduce cardiac reserve, especially in stiff ventricles, valve disease, or heart failure.
Sustained high ventricular rate and irregular activation can impair ventricular systolic function and provoke pulmonary edema or heart failure decompensation.

latent_mechanisms.display_name: Left atrial appendage stasis and thromboembolism
latent_mechanisms.clinical_meaning: Atrial mechanical dysfunction and stasis, amplified by patient thromboembolic substrate, promote left atrial appendage thrombus and embolic events.
Thyroid dysfunction, electrolyte disturbance, alcohol exposure, acute systemic illness, postoperative stress, ischemia, hypoxemia, or stimulant tone can lower the threshold for atrial fibrillation.
A hidden recovery capacity determined by atrial remodeling burden, episode duration, trigger reversibility, atrial size, and rhythm-control substrate.

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: Shorter duration, smaller atrium, and reversible trigger dominance improve durable rhythm response.
Appendage thrombus changes the risk balance of immediate rhythm transition.

treatments.context_specific_role: Rapid rhythm reshape vector that can immediately reduce AF activity and rate-related instability when rhythm transition succeeds.

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: Poor perfusion reserve limits nodal-slowing benefit.
Adrenergic excess makes sympathetic rate control more relevant.

treatments.context_specific_role: Rate-control push vector that lowers ventricular response and downstream hemodynamic stress without directly eliminating the AF substrate.

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: Systolic dysfunction can make negative inotropy less tolerated.

treatments.context_specific_role: AV nodal slowing vector for rapid AF where blood pressure and ventricular systolic reserve can tolerate it.

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: High adrenergic tone can blunt digoxin rate control.
Electrolyte disturbance changes digoxin safety.

treatments.context_specific_role: Rate-control vector with slower onset and context-dependent utility when hypotension limits stronger nodal-slowing push.

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: Thyroid context changes long-term amiodarone risk.

treatments.context_specific_role: Rhythm and partial rate-control reshape vector whose benefit and toxicity depend on substrate, urgency, and endocrine context.

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: Structural substrate changes class IC safety.

treatments.context_specific_role: Rhythm-control reshape vector for trigger-dominant AF when structural and ischemic risk context is low.

quality_checks: Pure disease-name-only distillation scope: Atrial fibrillation.
No real case search, no real case reading, and no staged real-case files were used for this disease file.
AF is represented as a first-layer disease leaf; temporal pattern, valvular context, triggers, substrate, embolic risk, and treatment feasibility are axes or modifiers.
Exactly one derived_hazard axis is present: mortality_hazard_in_D-ATRIAL-FIBRILLATION.
Treatment fields avoid ranking labels; rate, rhythm, embolic, bleeding, heart-failure, and procedural effects should emerge from forward simulation.

Parent/satellite structure separates ECG parent findings, AF morphology, rate response, symptoms, hemodynamics, structural substrate, trigger context, treatment modifiers, event hazards, and mortality hazard.
